headline: Binance still says withdrawals restart today, Sunday 1 Nov, but its latest updates gave no time.

stories.title: Binance withdrawals due today, Sunday 1 Nov, still with no time given
stories.summary: Binance says it has replaced about 90% of the crypto taken in the hack and is on track to restart withdrawals on Sunday 1 Nov, with details to come once confirmed. It took money from its SAFU user-protection fund to help cover the gap. The full Proof of Reserves (a public check that customer balances are fully backed) is now expected on 3 Nov.
points: Binance says it has replenished 90% of the roughly $6.3B stolen, up from 80%, and says it will absorb the loss, not its users, per CoinDesk.
Ten tokens are 100% backed: BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC. The rest, less-liquid tokens, is being bought on the market and in private (OTC) deals, per CoinDesk.
Binance moved 7,499 BTC out of SAFU, worth about $581M according to Whale Alert, per Cryptonomist.
Withdrawals are still expected to resume on Sunday 1 Nov as planned, per TokenPost; no hour has been announced.
Proof of Reserves: the snapshot was taken at 00:00 UTC 31 Oct and the full report is due on 3 Nov UTC, per TokenPost.

stories.title: Hacker funds are being laundered around the clock as October ends lower
stories.summary: Elliptic says the stolen funds on the Tron network are moving out every hour like a programmed routine, while CoinDesk says the 18,270 stolen bitcoin has not been spent. US spot bitcoin and ether funds saw heavy outflows into the end of October, and bitcoin was down about 7.4% for the month shortly before the close.
points: Elliptic says the main Tron wallet sent funds every hour for 31 hours straight, about $93.5M to some 150 wallets, with routes including THORChain ($25M).
Total stolen: Elliptic says $6.43B, Binance about $6.3B. Frozen: Elliptic has verified $2.84B; Binance says about $3B.
The 18,270 stolen BTC sits in 19 addresses and none had been spent in CoinDesk's latest check; that is more than Tesla's 11,509 BTC, per CoinDesk.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had $643.2M of net outflows on 30 Oct, the worst day since late June; spot ether ETFs had their 11th straight day of outflows, per 24/7 Wall St.
Before the monthly close, FinanceFeeds had bitcoin down about 7.4% for October.

stories.title: Midterms on Tuesday put the stalled crypto bill in focus
stories.summary: The US votes on Tuesday 3 Nov. Crypto groups have spent heavily on the races, hoping a new Congress will pass the CLARITY Act, the market-structure bill that stalled in the Senate in September.
points: Reuters counted about $176M of crypto-linked election spending across more than 100 races, per crypto.news; Fairshake and its affiliates account for about $150.8M.
The CLARITY Act passed the House 294-134 in July 2025, but a Senate vote to start debate failed 49-50 on 15 Sep 2026, short of the 60 needed, per crypto.news.
Main sticking points: ethics rules for the president, stablecoin rewards and protections for DeFi developers, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Stablecoin freezes cut the hacker's haul
briefs.summary: Tether froze about $1.567B of USDT and Circle about $823M of USDC; the attacker had swapped about $786M of stablecoins into ETH and TRX first, per FinanceFeeds.

briefs.title: Centralization cut both ways
briefs.summary: CoinDesk argues central control made the hack possible but freezes by Tether and Circle also saved about $3B.

briefs.title: Ether funds keep bleeding
briefs.summary: Spot ether ETFs had their 11th straight day of outflows on 30 Oct, about $1.61B for October, per 24/7 Wall St.

briefs.title: Big bitcoin options expiry next Friday
briefs.summary: About $2.065B of bitcoin options expire on Fri 6 Nov, with a put/call ratio of 0.32, per TokenPost.
